instruction.text: Jeremy is asking his teacher why we have to eat food. Fill in the gaps in her responses.

atoms.b: Mrs Jones, why do we have to eat food every day?
atoms.sound: Mrs Jones, why do we have to eat food every day?

atoms.b: We need to eat food to convert it into ((++energy oxygen)). Unlike ((++plants fish)), we can’t make our own energy, so we need to get it from different types of food.
atoms.sound: We need to eat food to convert it into energy. Unlike plants, we can’t make our own energy, so we need to get it from different types of food.

atoms.b: How do we know how much of each food to eat?
atoms.sound: How do we know how much of each food to eat?

atoms.b: We need ((++different the_same)) amounts of food each day depending on lots of different factors. For example, our age, size, gender, and how much we ((++move_about blink)) during the day. A 6-foot-tall athlete will need much ((++more less)) food than a 2-year-old toddler.
atoms.sound: We need different amounts of food each day depending on lots of different factors. For example, our age, size, gender and how much we move about during the day. A 6-foot-tall athlete will need much more food than a 2-year-old toddler.

instruction.text: Read the sentences and decide if they are true or false.

atoms.a: Humans need to eat to get energy.
All humans need to eat the same amount of food each day to get the right amount of nutrients.

end.text: That’s right, everyone needs a different amount of food.

instruction.text: Continue to fill in the gaps in the conversation.

atoms.b: Can we sort the food we eat into different categories?
atoms.sound: Can we sort the food we eat into different categories?

atoms.b: We can split food into 4 main categories which all give us different benefits: carbohydrates; fruits and vegetables; ((++proteins sauces)); and ((++fats_and_sugars berries)).
atoms.sound: We can split food into 4 main categories which all give us different benefits: carbohydrates; fruits and vegetables; proteins; and fats and sugars.

atoms.b: So if I eat an equal amount of food from each category, I will have a balanced diet?
atoms.sound: So if I eat an equal amount of food from each category, I will have a balanced diet?

atoms.b: Actually, we need ((++different equal)) amounts of food from each category. There is something called the food pyramid that helps us visualise how much of each category we should be eating to maintain a ((++balanced unhealthy)) diet.
atoms.sound: Actually, we need different amounts of food from each category. There is something called the food pyramid that helps us visualise how much of each category we should be eating to maintain a balanced diet.

instruction.text: Choose the correct label for the layer of the food pyramid.

feedback.end: The food pyramid represents how much of each food group we should eat each day. The bigger the layer, the bigger the portion. Not every meal has to be perfectly balanced, but it’s good to aim for your days and weeks to be balanced.
